_comment: FC-1 INC-2 gate (a), CONVERGED window.  50-station GPS+Galileo all-on golden posture,
30 s, 3 h (361 epochs inclusive), COLD start at 00:00 DOY-129, fast_clock in SHADOW.
WHY 3 h and not the 11-epoch smoke: the 11-epoch shadow measured the producer's own
per-epoch satellite-clock change at 0.3-3.7 m (common-mode removed, and unchanged by
detrending), against 1-2.5 cm of physically-measured phase change, with correlation
~0.  Cold-start churn is documented at 20-40x its converged level, so an 11-epoch
window cannot separate 'the producer churns' from 'the producer is still converging'.
This run grades hr0 against hr2 to settle that, which is the input the INC-4 verdict
depends on: if the producer's clock churn stays orders above the physical clock
motion once converged, then no fast tier can beat ZOH against it, because what ZOH
fails to predict is the churn and the fast tier measures the physics.
Shadow only — no decimation, no emission.  Estimation outputs stay byte-identical to
the same config with the tier off (the INC-0/INC-1 isolation gate).
